clauses.reason: Exhausted by performance when issued. The order revokes Executive Order No. 2987 of November 4, 1918 and returns the land to the Governor of The Panama Canal, with no deferred effective date, so the revocation operated on April 25, 1942, the date line of the order. Alternative reading: effect began on Federal Register filing, April 27, 1942 (F.R. Doc. 42-3733). Actor: EO 9147 itself.

research_rationale:
EO 9147 (April 25, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt), titled Revocation of Executive Order No. 2987 of November 4, 1918, Placing Certain Land and Water Areas Under the Jurisdiction of the Secretary of Navy for Use as a Naval Air Station, Canal Zone, read in full in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9147.txt; 7 FR 3111, PDF pages 1-1; machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF). The order has one operative command: under section 5 of title 2 of the Canal Zone Code and as President, it revokes Executive Order No. 2987 of November 4, 1918, which placed land and water areas in Gatun Lake, Canal Zone, under the control of the Secretary of the Navy for use as a Naval Air Station, and returns the land to the control and jurisdiction of the Governor of The Panama Canal. It states no deferred effective date and no condition. First end: the revocation operated when the order was issued, so the command was exhausted by performance on the order's date, 1942-04-25. The alternative reading that effect began on Federal Register filing (the text records F.R. Doc. 42-3733 filed April 27, 1942) is stated; the text itself gives no basis for deferral. The text of EO 2987 itself was not read; the identity of the revoked order rests on the recital in EO 9147.
